ctx_read.when_to_use: Reading source files with automatic compression mode selection. Default starting point for any file read.
ctx_read.when_not_to_use: When you need to read multiple files at once (use ctx_multi_read) or need raw grep results (use ctx_search).
ctx_read.token_impact: 74-99% savings depending on mode. Re-reads from cache cost ~13 tokens.

examples.title: Auto-mode read (default)
examples.description: lean-ctx selects the best compression mode automatically based on file size, recency, and task context.

examples.title: Force full read
examples.description: Returns complete file content. Use when editing or when you need every detail.

examples.title: Read specific line range
examples.description: Surgical read of lines 42-80 only. Minimal token cost.

ctx_shell.when_to_use: Running any shell command with automatic output compression. Replaces native terminal tools.
ctx_shell.when_not_to_use: For long-running processes (dev servers) - those should be run natively. Also skip for simple file reads (use ctx_read).
ctx_shell.token_impact: 60-95% output compression for common tools (git, npm, cargo, docker, ls, find, etc.)

examples.title: Git status with compression
examples.description: Output is automatically compressed by the git pattern module.

examples.title: Raw output (skip compression)
examples.description: Returns uncompressed output. Use when you need exact formatting.

ctx_search.when_to_use: Finding code patterns across files with regex. Faster than reading entire files when looking for specific code.
ctx_search.when_not_to_use: For semantic/meaning-based search (use ctx_semantic_search) or when you know exactly which file (use ctx_read).
ctx_search.token_impact: ~1200 tokens saved vs reading full files for typical search results.

ctx_tree.when_to_use: Exploring project structure. Great at session start or when navigating unfamiliar codebases.
ctx_tree.when_not_to_use: When you need file contents (use ctx_read) or when you know the exact path already.
ctx_tree.token_impact: Compact tree output vs listing all files individually.

ctx_agent.when_to_use: Multi-agent workflows where multiple AI editors need to coordinate, share findings, or hand off tasks.
ctx_agent.when_not_to_use: Single-agent sessions where you're the only AI working on the project.
ctx_agent.token_impact: Agent registration adds ~50 tokens. Diary entries persist across sessions.

ctx_session.when_to_use: Persisting task context across chat sessions. Recording key findings and decisions for later recovery. The reset action also clears the context ledger for a complete fresh start.
ctx_session.when_not_to_use: For short, one-off questions that don't need persistence.
ctx_session.token_impact: Session load recovers full context in ~200-500 tokens instead of re-reading files.

ctx_ledger.when_to_use: Managing context pressure. Check current pressure status, reset the ledger to clear accumulated pressure, or evict specific paths that are no longer needed.
ctx_ledger.when_not_to_use: When context pressure is low and manageable. For session-wide resets, use ctx_session reset instead (which also clears the ledger).
ctx_ledger.token_impact: Eviction reduces tracked token usage immediately. Reset clears all accumulated pressure to zero.

examples.title: Check current pressure
examples.description: Shows current token usage, entry count, and pressure percentage.

examples.title: Evict specific files
examples.description: Removes specified paths from the ledger and adds exclusion overlays to prevent re-accumulation.

examples.title: Full reset
examples.description: Clears all ledger entries and resets pressure to zero. Use when starting a new task focus.

ctx_gain.when_to_use: Checking how many tokens lean-ctx saved in the current session. Useful for reporting and optimization.
ctx_gain.when_not_to_use: During active development - checking gain too often wastes tokens itself.

ctx_preload.when_to_use: At session start - give it your task description and it auto-loads relevant files into cache.
ctx_preload.when_not_to_use: When you already know exactly which files to read (use ctx_read directly).
ctx_preload.token_impact: Pre-loads 3-8 files in optimal modes, saving individual read roundtrips.

ctx_overview.when_to_use: First call in a new session - gives project structure, key files, and entry points in one call.
ctx_overview.when_not_to_use: When you already have context from a previous session (use ctx_session load instead).
ctx_overview.token_impact: One call replaces 3-5 individual reads for orientation.

ctx_workflow.when_to_use: Managing multi-step workflows with state machines - enforces step ordering and evidence collection.
ctx_workflow.when_not_to_use: Simple tasks without multiple stages. Overhead isn't worth it for quick fixes.
ctx_workflow.token_impact: Workflow state tracking adds ~50-100 tokens per transition.

ctx_execute.when_to_use: Running code snippets in a sandboxed environment (11 languages). Safe execution without affecting the project.
ctx_execute.when_not_to_use: For shell commands (use ctx_shell) or when you need to modify project files (use ctx_edit).

ctx_knowledge.when_to_use: Storing and recalling project-specific knowledge - patterns, gotchas, conventions that persist across sessions.
ctx_knowledge.when_not_to_use: For temporary findings (use ctx_session finding instead).
ctx_knowledge.token_impact: Knowledge recall costs ~20-50 tokens. Saves full re-discovery across sessions.

ctx_callgraph.when_to_use: Unified entry point for caller/callee analysis when tracing impact of code changes.
ctx_callgraph.when_not_to_use: When you need full architecture graphs (use ctx_graph or ctx_architecture).
ctx_callgraph.token_impact: Focused call-chain output avoids broad graph reads and reduces context volume.

ctx_expand.when_to_use: Inspecting compressed checkpoints or archived context blocks during long-running sessions.
ctx_expand.when_not_to_use: For normal file reads or search operations (use ctx_read/ctx_search).
ctx_expand.token_impact: Restores only selected archived chunks instead of reloading full session context.

ctx_review.when_to_use: Generating a structured review packet (impact, callers, tests, checklist) before merge.
ctx_review.when_not_to_use: When you only need one narrow lookup like a symbol search.
ctx_review.token_impact: Bundles multiple review steps into one tool call to avoid repeated exploratory reads.

ctx_smells.when_to_use: Detecting code smells like long functions, deep nesting, and high complexity. Uses property graph for dependency-aware scoring.
ctx_smells.when_not_to_use: When you need detailed AST analysis (use ctx_outline) or dependency graphs (use ctx_architecture).
ctx_smells.token_impact: Returns compact smell report with graph-enriched scores.

ctx_discover_tools.when_to_use: Finding available lean-ctx tools by keyword when you don't know the exact tool name. Useful for on-demand tool loading in lazy clients.
ctx_discover_tools.when_not_to_use: When you already know which tool to use. Use ctx_call to invoke tools directly.
ctx_discover_tools.token_impact: Minimal — returns matching tool names and descriptions only.
